summary: Adalbert Kuhn worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin (1833–1837) and served at Köllnisches Gymnasium as teacher, professor, and director (1837, 1841, 1856, 1870).

Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at La Trobe University under Greg Bailey by 2004 and is attested as senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland from 2016 to 2018.

Adam Hardy specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. After studying architecture at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1971–1974), he held professorships at De Montfort University (~1993–2005) and Cardiff University (~2005).

Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, and studied with numerous traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama.

Adam Yuet Chau is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Williams College and completed his PhD at Stanford University (2001), later serving as university lecturer (attested 2011–2015) and Professor of the Anthropology of China (attested 2026) at Cambridge.
Adele Schlombs is a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. She held a post at the Museum für Ostasiatische Kunst Köln from ~1991 to 2022.

Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, and Marburg, and held posts as guest professor at the University of Vienna (~2004) and Privatdozentin at the University of Marburg (2009).

Adelheid Mette was an Indologist who studied at the University of Hamburg (1953–1958, Habilitation by 1972). She held professorships at the University of Munich (1978, 1980) and served as chair of Indology at the University of Münster (1988–2000).

Aden Kumler is an art historian who studied at Chicago, Toronto, Harvard (PhD ~1999–2007), and the Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies. She served as assistant professor at the University of Chicago (2007) and became professor at the University of Basel (2020).
Adeu Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under Samten Gyatso and Chögon Rinpoche.

Adhémard Leclère worked in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as Résident de France at Kratie in the French Protectorate of Cambodia and was vice-president of the Société Ethnologique de Paris, which he founded.

Adinath Neminath Upadhye was an Indologist educated at the University of Mumbai (BA ~1926–1930, D.Litt. ~1930–1939). He taught at Rajaram College (1930–1962), was Professor Emeritus at Shivaji University (1962–1971), and headed the Jaina Chair at Mysore (1971).

Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Bopp, Schlegel, Lassen, and Sacy, earning a PhD at Berlin (1826–1829). He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Breslau (1833–1847) and its rector (1862–1863).

Adolf Holtzmann worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Berlin, Munich under Frank and Schmeller (~1834–1837), and Paris under Burnouf (~1839–1840), later serving as professor of German literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University (1852–1870).

Adolf Kaegi was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Zurich, Leipzig, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. From 1875 he taught at the University of Zurich, serving as full professor of Sanskrit and classical philology (1893–1914).

Adolf Kiessling studied under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1856–1858). He held academic posts at the University of Basel (~1869–1872), the University of Greifswald (~1872–1889), and the University of Göttingen (~1889–1893).

Adolf Kirchhoff worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1842–1846) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh, later serving at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium (1846) and as ordinary professor at Frederick William University Berlin (from 1865).
Adolf Noreen was a linguist who studied at Uppsala University (~1871–1877) and under August Leskien (~1879). He held an academic post at Uppsala University from ~1877 to 1919.

Adolphe Regnier worked in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology, having studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held posts at the Collège de France (1838), the École Normale Supérieure (1841–1843), and served as librarian at the Palace of Fontainebleau (1873).

Adriaan Scharpé was an Indologist who earned his doctoral degree at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1935–1937). He subsequently held posts at the University of Amsterdam (1947–1978) and Ghent University (~1948–1983).
